cognition.elementary: I'm really glad you told me. What you're feeling matters, and you don't have to handle it alone. Please tell a grown-up you trust right now, like a parent, your teacher, or the school counselor. If you might be in danger, call 911. You can also call or text 988 to talk to someone whose job is helping kids.
cognition.default: I'm really glad you told me, and I'm sorry you're carrying this. You deserve support from a person, not just a study tool. Please reach out today to someone you trust, like a parent, teacher, or school counselor. You can call or text 988 (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline) any time, and if you are in immediate danger, call 911.

behavior.elementary: Thank you for telling me. You matter, and you deserve help to feel better. Please tell a grown-up you trust right away, like a parent, your teacher, or the school counselor. If you are hurt or in danger, call 911. You can also call or text 988.
behavior.default: Thank you for telling me. You deserve care and support with this, and you don't have to deal with it alone. Please talk to someone you trust today, like a parent, teacher, or school counselor. You can call or text 988 any time, and if you are hurt or in danger, call 911.

disclosure.elementary: Thank you for telling me. It is not your fault, and you deserve to be safe. Please tell a grown-up you trust, like your teacher or the school counselor, as soon as you can. You can also call the Childhelp hotline at 1-800-422-4453. If you are in danger right now, call 911.
disclosure.default: Thank you for telling me. What you described is not your fault, and you deserve to be safe. Please tell a trusted adult, like a teacher or school counselor, as soon as you can. You can also call the Childhelp National Child Abuse Hotline at 1-800-422-4453, and if you are in danger right now, call 911.

mid.elementary: That sounds really hard, and it's okay to feel that way. Talking to a grown-up you trust, like a parent or your teacher, can help a lot. I'm here to help with your schoolwork whenever you're ready.
mid.default: That sounds really hard, and it makes sense to feel that way sometimes. Talking it through with someone you trust, like a friend, parent, teacher, or school counselor, can really help. I'm here to help with your schoolwork whenever you're ready.

check_in.elementary: Before we keep going: how are you feeling? If something is bothering you, it's okay to talk to a grown-up you trust.
check_in.default: Before we keep going, I want to check in: how are you doing? If something is weighing on you, talking to someone you trust can help.

templates.blocked_response: I can't give that answer. Let's get back to your question, or you can ask it in a different way.

classifier.note: Classifier-only high escalates on its own at >= strong_high; between high and strong_high it needs a second signal (rule or anchor), otherwise it becomes a check-in. strong_high was set after seeing fresh3.

context_downgrade.note: A rule-only hit inside an educational or play framing becomes a check-in (never nothing), unless the semantic layer or the classifier independently says high.

context_downgrade.accident: \b(?:while (?:cooking|cutting|chopping|shaving|baking|playing|running)|on (?:the|a) (?:stove|oven|pan|paper|knife)|by accident|accidentally|how (?:do|should) i (?:clean|treat|bandage|care for)|does (?:that|it) need a bandage|paper cut)\b

multi_turn.note: Risk that builds across turns is upgraded; after a high, the session stays escalated and later replies must keep a person in the loop for a few turns.

audit.note: Every non-allow decision is appended as one JSON line. Message text is logged so a person can follow up; switch off with log_message_text=false where policy requires.

output_filter.note: Applied to what the pipeline returns to K-12 learners: explicit, instructional or graphic adult content is blocked.
